purpose: FireOpsSim authored company drill library. Training aids must be adapted to department SOP/SOGs, staffing, apparatus, facilities, adopted standards and manufacturer guidance.

drills.title: Attack Line Deployment & Advancement
drills.goal: Deploy, charge and advance the department attack package efficiently while maintaining nozzle control, hose management and crew communication.
objectives: Select an appropriate line for the stated problem
Coordinate water, nozzle and backup positions
Advance while managing corners and hose movement
setup: Create a safe simulated entry point and travel path
Use the department's normal attack package
Assign nozzle, backup and operator/door roles
evolution: Give an occupancy and simulated fire location without prescribing the stretch
Crew selects and deploys the line
Call for water and perform department nozzle readiness checks
performance: No uncontrolled hose movement or avoidable kinks
criticalErrors: Unsafe hose charging or uncontrolled movement
Action conflicts with department safety procedure
drills.remediation: Reduce the evolution to deployment, water call and first 25 feet of advancement; coach the failed component and repeat before restoring complexity.
drills.advanced: Add a changing fire location or second assignment requiring the crew to communicate and adapt.
aar: Where did the stretch lose time?
What made advancement easier or harder?
Was communication early enough?
What one change should be retained?
drills.outcome: Crew can repeatedly place an operational attack line from apparatus to target without step-by-step prompting.
sources: FSRI fire dynamics and suppression training

drills.title: Primary Search — Known Victim Location
drills.goal: Locate and remove a reported victim while integrating entry selection, isolation, ventilation decisions, suppression progress and communications.
objectives: Choose an entry point based on conditions and victim information
Select an effective victim removal path
setup: Place a mannequin at a known reported location
Establish safe boundaries and emergency stop signal
Brief suppression progress as scenario information rather than prescribing search actions
evolution: Provide arrival conditions and reported victim location
Crew selects entry and search plan
Crew decides isolation/ventilation/removal actions and completes removal
performance: Communication reflects conditions and suppression progress
Removal route is deliberate rather than automatic
criticalErrors: Loss of crew integrity without recognition
Continuing through an instructor-declared unsafe condition
drills.remediation: Return to a single-room search with known victim location and explicit orientation checkpoints, then repeat the decision point.
drills.advanced: Run simultaneous suppression and search crews with separate information and require coordination.
aar: Why did you choose that entry?
What changed your isolation or ventilation decision?
How did suppression progress affect the search?
Was the removal path still best when conditions changed?
drills.outcome: Crew makes and communicates search decisions from fire conditions and victim information rather than following an automatic sequence.

drills.title: Mayday Recognition & Radio Discipline
drills.goal: Recognize a firefighter emergency early and initiate the department Mayday procedure without instructor prompting.
setup: Use a non-IDLH scenario
Confirm department Mayday procedure and radio emergency-button behavior before training
Assign firefighter, command/controller and other radio roles
evolution: Give the firefighter a normal task
Introduce a safe simulated disorientation, separation, entrapment or air emergency
Do not tell the member to call a Mayday
performance: Emergency alert feature used according to local procedure
Command acknowledges and controls radio traffic
criticalErrors: Instructor allows scenario to exceed established safety limits
drills.remediation: Practice recognition and radio message from a stationary tabletop scenario before repeating movement-based training.
drills.advanced: Add multiple operating crews and a separate RIT/RIC assignment to create controlled radio congestion.
aar: What was the trigger to declare?
Was any important information delayed?
Did command ask for information already transmitted?
How can radio overload be reduced?
drills.outcome: Members recognize locally defined emergency conditions and execute the department Mayday communications process reliably.

drills.title: SCBA Emergency Procedures & Air Awareness
drills.goal: Build familiarity with SCBA status, air awareness and department/manufacturer emergency procedures in a controlled training environment.
objectives: Demonstrate equipment-specific emergency actions from approved training
Exit or transition according to department procedure
setup: Inspect the training area and prop
Establish instructor-to-student ratio and emergency stop procedure
Use only department/manufacturer-approved techniques
evolution: Member identifies, communicates and follows trained procedure
Terminate and reset before introducing another problem
performance: Member does not improvise a hazardous technique
criticalErrors: Restricted movement or prop creates uncontrolled entrapment
Training continues after distress or stop signal
drills.remediation: Return to seated equipment familiarization and verbal walk-through before another evolution.
drills.advanced: Add a radio communication task while maintaining conservative physical workload and instructor control.
aar: What first indicated the problem?
What information should your partner/command receive?
What action is equipment-specific?
When should the evolution be terminated?
drills.outcome: Member demonstrates equipment familiarity and safe response to simulated SCBA problems.

drills.title: Ground Ladder Selection, Raise & Placement
drills.goal: Select and place the appropriate ladder for a stated fireground objective rather than merely repeating a memorized raise.
objectives: Select ladder based on objective and reach
Place for rescue, access or egress objective
setup: Choose multiple safe target points
Mark overhead hazards if none naturally exist
Assign tip/base roles as locally used
evolution: Give an objective such as rescue, roof access or secondary egress
Instructor changes objective and crew repeats
injects: Change from rescue to roof access
drills.remediation: Practice selection and placement discussion without raising, then perform one coached raise.
drills.advanced: Add limited staffing or require two ladders for separate tactical objectives.
aar: Why this ladder?
Was placement correct for the objective?
Where did communication break down?
How would staffing change the operation?
drills.outcome: Crew selects and places ground ladders based on tactical need and local technique.

drills.title: Tank-to-Sustained Water Supply Transition
drills.goal: Establish a dependable water supply and transition from tank water while maintaining assigned fire flow.
setup: Define target attack-line flow and safe operating area
Use department hose and hydrant/water-source procedure
Assign operator and supply roles
evolution: Begin simulated/actual attack from tank as approved
Confirm intake, tank and discharge conditions
performance: Attack supply remains stable within training limits
drills.remediation: Practice the transition sequence without flowing, then repeat with one line and no injects.
drills.advanced: Add a second line or limited-supply scenario consistent with department hydraulics training.
aar: What indicated it was time to transition?
What changed at intake/discharge?
Where could communication cause failure?
How would reduced staffing affect the plan?
drills.outcome: Operator can transition to sustained supply predictably while maintaining situational awareness.
sources: Department driver/operator practices; pair with FireOps Calc for hydraulics practice

drills.title: First-Due Size-Up & Initial Action Plan
drills.goal: Produce a concise arrival report, identify the highest-priority problem and communicate an achievable initial action plan.
objectives: Update the plan when conditions change
setup: Select a local building photo or FireOpsSim scenario image
Prepare a second condition/information reveal
Assign first-due officer and incoming resources
evolution: Officer gives arrival report and initial plan using local command language
Officer updates plan and communicates changes
performance: Plan changes when new information warrants it
criticalErrors: Assignment knowingly exceeds scenario staffing/capability without correction
drills.remediation: Pause the radio component and have member state observations, priorities and assignments separately before recombining them.
drills.advanced: Run multi-company tabletop with each role receiving different information.
aar: What fact drove your first decision?
What information was missing?
Was the assignment realistic?
What trigger changed your plan?
drills.outcome: Officer converts limited arrival information into a clear initial plan and adapts as conditions evolve.

drills.title: Post-Fire Gross Decontamination & Clean Transport
drills.goal: Reduce transfer of fireground contamination from PPE to skin, apparatus, station and personal environments using department-approved exposure-reduction practices.
objectives: Bag and transport contaminated gear appropriately
setup: Use clean training gear or simulated contamination
Lay out department decon supplies
Identify clean and dirty zones
evolution: Practice controlled doffing and skin-cleaning sequence
Bag gear and identify appropriate apparatus transport/storage location
performance: Gear bagged/handled according to local procedure
criticalErrors: Using a training process that damages PPE or violates manufacturer guidance
injects: Member prepares to place dirty gear in cab
drills.remediation: Walk through the clean/dirty path with clean PPE and labeled zones before repeating the complete sequence.
drills.advanced: Have an officer design a post-fire workflow for the department's actual apparatus and station.
aar: Where is cross-contamination most likely?
What should remain out of the passenger compartment?
How does your station isolate dirty gear?
What local step needs improvement?
drills.outcome: Crew can move from suppression through preliminary exposure reduction without unnecessarily spreading contamination.
sources: NIOSH Protecting Firefighters from Contaminated Gear, 2026

drills.title: Unresponsive Firefighter — PPE/SCBA Removal Transition
equipment: training mannequin or consenting training member per local policy
drills.goal: Practice the department-approved transition from firefighter rescue to rapid access for medical care when a firefighter is unresponsive.
objectives: Recognize need for rapid transition to medical care
Remove/adjust PPE and SCBA using department-approved training technique
setup: Use NIOSH guidance and department medical/rescue procedure
Assign safety officer/controller
Use a mannequin when appropriate to avoid unnecessary trainee risk
evolution: Crew moves to a safe treatment area as scenario requires
performance: Medical access is not unnecessarily delayed
Equipment handled without creating additional injury risk
criticalErrors: Unsafe compression/positioning of a live training participant
Training delays actual medical evaluation of a symptomatic member
drills.remediation: Practice the removal sequence slowly on a mannequin with instructor coaching before adding timing or scenario pressure.
drills.advanced: Integrate rescue team handoff to EMS and command communications.
aar: What slowed access to the patient?
Were roles clear?
What equipment created difficulty?
How should fire and EMS functions integrate?
drills.outcome: Crew can transition an unresponsive firefighter to medical care using a rehearsed, coordinated process.

drills.title: District Building Construction Walkaround
drills.goal: Connect building construction and occupancy features to actual tactical decisions in the response district.
objectives: Discuss fire spread and collapse indicators
Connect features to water, ladder and forcible-entry needs
setup: Choose a building where the crew can observe legally and safely
Do not enter private/restricted areas without permission
Officer prepares 3–5 prompts
evolution: Each member identifies one operational feature before the officer teaches
performance: Members support observations with visible building features
Tactical discussion distinguishes facts from assumptions
criticalErrors: Entering restricted property or creating a public/traffic hazard
drills.remediation: Use a building photograph at the station and identify construction, access and tactical features with instructor prompts.
drills.advanced: Have an officer candidate deliver the walkaround and create a short company preplan discussion.
aar: What feature matters most at 02:00?
Where would apparatus go?
What would make search difficult?
What would you want dispatch/incoming companies to know?
drills.outcome: Members read buildings in their own district and translate observations into operational considerations.
